summary: The design has unresolved lifecycle, credential-isolation, installation, and image-pinning problems that prevent the stated cross-platform and hermetic guarantees from being implemented as written.

recommendations.location: Architecture: the container as the boundary; Python module layout (`sandbox.py`)
recommendations.issue: [P1] `docker run --rm` with no writable host mount cannot preserve the file produced by `-o <verdict-file>` after exit. Killing a timed-out Docker client also does not reliably terminate or remove the daemon-managed container, so the bounded-run guarantee is incomplete.
recommendations.suggestion: Define a concrete lifecycle that retains the container ID, attaches with bounded stdout/stderr capture, explicitly kills it on timeout, copies the verdict before removal, and removes it in a guaranteed cleanup path. Alternatively, specify and validate a bounded, unambiguous output-framing protocol that returns the verdict separately from JSONL.

recommendations.issue: [P1] Mounting host `~/.codex` read-only exposes every file in that directory, directly contradicting the claim that only `auth.json` and `AGENTS.md` are exposed. Read-only prevents mutation, not disclosure, and any force-enabled capability control running under the Codex UID could read the live credential. The container is therefore not an independent boundary around that secret.
recommendations.suggestion: Expose only validated regular files through individual mounts or a host-created minimal staging directory, define UID/permission and symlink handling, and never use the live credential in capability-enabled controls. Narrow the independence claim or introduce credential brokering that keeps the refresh credential outside the reviewer container.

recommendations.location: Installer & skill dispatch, steps 2–4; Premises / live-evidence
recommendations.issue: [P1] The installer requires current live-evidence before it runs the local schema gate and security battery. Because the invocation fingerprint includes the local runtime identity and run profile, a fresh machine or changed runtime will normally have no current evidence and will be refused before it can generate any.
recommendations.suggestion: Use a transactional bootstrap sequence: pin and fingerprint the stack, invalidate old evidence, run offline checks and both live gates, atomically record their successful evidence, revalidate the completed manifest, and only then install or publish.

recommendations.location: Overview; Platform matrix; The Codex image
recommendations.issue: [P1] “Same image” and “image digest” are underspecified for Apple Silicon and other multi-architecture hosts. An OCI index digest can select different architecture-specific manifests and binaries, while a local Docker image ID is a different identity again. Thus a Linux x86 verification does not establish the claimed macOS boundary, and the per-round comparison may pin the wrong object.
recommendations.suggestion: Define the exact OCI identity being pinned. Either mandate one platform with `--platform` and pin its child manifest digest, or record and verify the index digest, selected child-manifest digest, config/image ID, OS, and architecture separately. Key live evidence to the actually executed platform image.

recommendations.location: The credential (auth + AGENTS.md); Risks and mitigations
recommendations.issue: [P2] Discarding refreshed `auth.json` assumes refresh tokens remain reusable. If the provider rotates or invalidates refresh tokens, the first container refresh can invalidate the unchanged host credential, breaking later rounds and possibly host authentication; concurrent rounds can worsen this race.
recommendations.suggestion: Establish and test the pinned CLI/provider’s refresh-token semantics. If rotation is possible, use a locked host-side broker or an atomic, narrowly validated persistence mechanism, or mint a short-lived per-round credential before launching the sandbox.

recommendations.location: The security battery, items 2 and 4; Network egress
recommendations.issue: [P2] A single invisible canary does not prove that no other host path or runtime socket was mounted, and checking only whether `auth.json` appears in the verdict does not cover JSONL, stderr, diagnostics, or arbitrary open-egress disclosure. These tests do not support the stated confidentiality proof.
recommendations.suggestion: Verify the actual runtime mount/device/socket table via runtime inspection and in-container mount information against an exact allowlist, including absence of Docker/Podman sockets. Audit every captured output channel for synthetic secrets, and explicitly scope the guarantee to a trusted pinned CLI/runtime unless network mediation is added.

recommendations.location: Behavioral equivalence requirements; Testing strategy, item 4
recommendations.issue: [P2] One equivalence fixture is insufficient to enforce byte-for-byte normalization and state compatibility across PowerShell and Python serializers, especially for Unicode escaping, key ordering, newline conventions, malformed values, and numeric boundaries.
recommendations.suggestion: Create a shared golden corpus covering all verdict and state artifacts, edge-case Unicode and escaping, bounds, failure cases, and carry-over transitions; run both implementations against it and byte-compare outputs in cross-platform CI.
